results.summary_before: This design is a characterization platform for a single external memristor or RRAM device, providing DC sweep, pulse endurance, retention, and free-running modes. It uses an 8-bit DAC to drive the device and an 8-bit ADC to read back the response, with SPI control for mode selection and data readout. The design includes on-chip histogram and min/max tracking for DC sweeps, and read-verify with fail-index latching for endurance tests. It is implemented as a mixed-signal design and requires an external resistive-switching device and SPI host.
results.summary: This design implements an 8-bit saturating leaky-integrate-and-fire neuron with a stochastic firing mode, an 8-entry sigmoid LUT, an 8-bit Galois LFSR, programmable refractory and leak, and homeostatic theta adaptation. It also includes an STDP controller with 8-bit pre and post spike traces, exponential-shift decay, an anti-Hebbian polarity bit, and optional reward-gated learning. All registers are programmable through a shared 8-bit SPI mode-0 slave, and the design emits spike, weight-update, theta, Bayesian confidence, learning-direction and busy outputs. It is written in Verilog and requires only an external SPI host and a spike-train source.

results.summary: This project implements a tiny FABulous FPGA fabric with 128 LUT4 plus flip-flop logic cells and a vertical carry chain for fast additions up to 15 bits. The I/Os resemble the Tiny Tapeout interface, allowing simple Tiny Tapeout designs to be mapped directly onto the fabric. User designs are synthesized with Yosys and implemented with nextpnr, and the bitstream is uploaded through a bitbang interface while reset is applied. The design is written in Verilog and includes cocotb tests, with no external hardware required.

It reuses building blocks from the original implementation and is intended for educational or retro-computing purposes. The design requires a microcontroller to drive the pins and no other external hardware. It is written in Amaranth and targets the Tiny Tapeout ASIC shuttle.
results.summary: This design implements a 2x2 output-stationary systolic array that computes signed 4-bit matrix multiplication and produces 8-bit results. Each processing element is a bit-serial multiply-accumulate unit, and the array uses input skew registers to align data across the grid. An FSM sequences the computation through IDLE, COMPUTE, DRAIN and READ states, and an output serializer streams the four accumulator results one per cycle. The design is written in Verilog and is loaded and started through the Tiny Tapeout input pins.

results.summary: This project implements a polyphonic MIDI synthesizer that decodes MIDI note messages and generates square waves for up to four voices. Each voice is routed to a separate output pin so the signals can be mixed externally, and each oscillator responds to a different MIDI channel to simplify voice allocation. A PWM output encodes the number of currently active voices and can be low-pass filtered to control the gain of the mixed output. The design is written in SystemVerilog and can drive a speaker through an external driver circuit.

results.summary_before: This design implements the wolf, goat and cabbage river crossing puzzle as a combinational logic block. Four input pins represent the positions of the farmer, wolf, goat and cabbage, and the outputs drive the segments of a 7-segment display to indicate a win, a loss, or which river bank has an unattended situation. The game is played interactively by setting the input pins to represent the positions of the four characters. The design is built with Wokwi and is intended for educational purposes.
